title: Accelerations during first 2s
description: Essential: Student must state both accelerations with correct magnitudes (8 m/s² for block, 2 m/s² for plank) and directions (block down incline, plank up incline).

title: Force analysis for accelerations
description: Important: Student must apply Newton's second law correctly to both block and plank, considering all friction forces and the applied force F.

title: Velocities at t=2s
description: Important: Student must calculate that both block and plank have speed 4 m/s at t=2s using kinematics with correct accelerations.

title: Relative displacement calculation
description: Essential: Student must compute the total relative displacement (Δx₁ + Δx₂ = 20.3 m) as the minimum board length.

title: Post-force removal analysis
description: Important: Student must analyze accelerations after force removal and determine when relative motion stops.

title: Friction direction confusion
description: Pitfall: Student incorrectly assigns direction of friction between block and plank (should oppose relative motion).

title: Sign errors in kinematics
description: Pitfall: Student uses wrong signs for velocities/accelerations when calculating relative displacements.

title: System approach check
description: Optional: Student verifies accelerations by considering the whole system or checking maximum static friction limits.
